elbphi: The concert hall on the harbour, built on top of an old brick warehouse, with a wave-shaped glass roof. The Plaza, the viewing deck at 37 metres, runs all round the building with a 360-degree view of the port, river and city.
speicher: The world's largest warehouse district on timber piles, a UNESCO site: red-brick buildings with turrets, canals (fleets) and bridges. Past the Wasserschloss, the water castle, the new HafenCity district leads to the Elbphilharmonie.
wunder: The world's largest model railway, inside a Speicherstadt warehouse: Italy, the United States, an airport with planes taking off, the Alps and Hamburg itself in miniature, with thousands of trains, cars and people. One of Hamburg's best-loved attractions, for adults and children alike.
rathaus: The neo-Renaissance city hall with its 112-metre tower and carved façades, overlooking the great Rathausmarkt square. A few steps away, the Jungfernstieg is the boulevard along the Binnenalster lake, with boats, swans and elegant buildings.
michel: The Baroque church with its 132-metre green copper tower is the symbol of the city. Inside, the white and gold nave is one of the most beautiful in the Lutheran north. From the platform on the tower, at 106 metres, you see the whole port.
nikolai: The Gothic tower of a church destroyed in the 1943 bombing, left standing as a memorial against war. In the crypt is an exhibition on the destruction of Hamburg; a panoramic lift takes you up to 76 metres.
landung: Landungsbrücken, Old Elbe Tunnel and harbour cruise

The floating piers from which the harbour boats leave, with the white "St. Pauli Landungsbrücken" lettering. From here you can walk under the river through the 1911 Old Elbe Tunnel, or take a harbour cruise among cranes, containers and ships.
reeper: Hamburg's world-famous entertainment street, in the St. Pauli district: theatres, live music, bars and neon lights. In the nearby lanes is Große Freiheit, where the Beatles got their start, and Davidstraße with the district's history.
kontor: The 1920s brick office district, a UNESCO site, with the Chilehaus, a building shaped like a ship's bow that seems to sail down the street. Expressionist architecture unique in Germany.
kunsthalle: Hamburg's great art museum, opposite the main station, with paintings from the Middle Ages to contemporary art: Caspar David Friedrich's Romantic landscapes (the "Wanderer above the Sea of Fog") are its most famous works, then Rembrandt, Monet and Munch.
planten: The green park in the centre, laid out on the old city walls, with a Japanese garden, flower greenhouses and a lake with a fountain. In the warm season there are evening water-and-light shows with music.
